articles.headline: WNBA championship and Finals MVP odds: Lynx head into playoffs as clear favorites
articles.description: The Lynx head into the WNBA playoffs as championship favorites, with Napheesa Collier and Olivia Miles the top picks for Finals MVP.

images.name: Olivia Miles [1296x729]
images.caption: Napheesa Collier, Olivia Miles and the Lynx remain big favorites to win the WNBA championship.
images.alt: Olivia Miles #5 of the Minnesota Lynx reacts to a foul call next to Napheesa Collier #24 during WNBA game against the Golden State Valkyries on August 19, 2026 at Chase Center in San Francisco, CA.

images.name: Napheesa Collier [1296x729]
images.caption: Napheesa Collier and the Lynx enter the week at even money to win the WNBA championship.
images.alt: Napheesa Collier #24 of the Minnesota Lynx drives to the basket during the game against the Las Vegas Aces on August 15, 2026 at Michelob ULTRA Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada.

images.name: Napheesa Collier [1296x729]
images.caption: Napheesa Collier, Natasha Howard and the Minnesota Lynx continue to roll.
images.alt: Napheesa Collier #24 of the Minnesota Lynx celebrates with teammate Natasha Howard #1 against the Toronto Tempo during the second half at Scotiabank Arena on July 30, 2026 in Toronto, Canada.

images.name: Napheesa Collier [1296x729]
images.caption: Napheesa Collier's welcome return only boosts a Lynx team that's the current favorite to win the WNBA Finals.
images.alt: Napheesa Collier #24 of the Minnesota Lynx shoots a free throw during the game against the Seattle Storm on July 22, 2026 at Climate Pledge Arena in Seattle, Washington.

images.name: Olivia Miles for Odds File (260720) [1296x729]
images.caption: Rookie of the Year front-runner Olivia Miles is one of the big reasons that the sportsbooks have made the Minnesota Lynx the team to beat for the championship this season.
images.alt: Olivia Miles #5 of the Minnesota Lynx looks on during the game against the Portland Fire on July 18, 2026 at Target Center in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

images.name: Gabby Williams  [1296x729]
images.caption: Gabby Williams leads the Valkyries in scoring with 15.0 PPG.
images.alt: Gabby Williams #1 of the Golden State Valkyries dribbles the ball during the game =a  on July 6, 2026 at  CareFirst Arena in Washington, D.C.

images.name: Olivia Miles [1296x729]
images.caption: Olivia Miles and the Minnesota Lynx are now alone in front as favorites to win the WNBA championship.
images.alt: Minnesota Lynx guard Olivia Miles (5) dribbles past Dallas Wings guard Azzi Fudd (35) during the WNBA game between the Dallas Wings and the Minnesota Lynx on June 28, 2026, at College Park Center in Arlington, TX.

images.name: Natasha Howard of Minnesota Lynx [608x342]
images.caption: A strong start to the season has the Lynx tied with the Aces for the shortest title odds, just ahead of the Liberty.

images.name: Olivia Miles [1296x729]
images.caption: The Lynx have seen their odds shorten but have a tough schedule this week.

images.caption: Rookie of the Year favorite Olivia Miles is helping drive the early success of the Minnesota Lynx.

articles.headline: Why Fever coach Stephanie White has the toughest job in sports
articles.description: She has the stars but also the strife. Stephanie White is fortifying her locker room as storms swirl around Indiana's championship hopes.

images.name: Stephanie White [1296x729]
images.caption: Stephanie White has been at the heart of a Fever season that has been both absurd and amazing. She hopes to bring it to an end with nine more wins.

images.name: Stephanie White Caitlin Clark [800x533]
images.caption: White's relationship with Caitlin Clark has been dissected throughout the season, most often on social media.

images.name: Stephanie White [800x450]
images.caption: Behind Caitlin Clark, Aliyah Boston and Kelsey Mitchell, White oversees the highest-scoring offense in the WNBA.

images.name: Stephanie White (Purdue) [1999x1999]
images.caption: White, playing under coach Carolyn Peck, celebrated a national championship at Purdue.

images.name: Stephanie White [800x800]
images.caption: White was booed by Fever fans in August after her comments on DiJonai Carrington's hard foul on Sophie Cunningham. "It hurt," White says. "But at the same time, I think it was a moment of realization that this is not what it used to be."

images.name: Briann January [800x800]
images.caption: Fever assistant Briann January, right, says White's focus this season has been keeping the team connected. "We have to stay strong, and we're strongest when we are together, when we're connected, and that's the whole thing," January says.

images.name: Stephanie White [800x533]
images.caption: White knows the Fever need to close their fists throughout the playoffs. Their title hopes depend on it.

images.name: Stephanie White says Fever 'will not be divided' in pregame media session
images.caption: WNBA Countdown's Malika Andrews, Andraya Carter and Chiney Ogwumike react to Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White's comments regarding the fallout from DiJonai Carrington's flagrant 2 foul on Sophie Cunningham.

articles.headline: Sun mark franchise's last game in Connecticut with victory, joy

article.story: LAS VEGAS -- — Four-time MVP A'ja Wilson scored 18 points and grabbed 10 rebounds to lead the Aces to an 89-79 victory over the Los Angeles Sparks on Tuesday night and clinch at least a No. 3 playoff seed for Las Vegas. The Aces (30-13), on a six-game winning streak, will get home-court advantage in the first round of the playoffs, which begin Sunday. If the standings hold, they would face No. 6 seed Washington (27-16) in the best-of-three series. Chelsea Gray scored 17 points of for the Aces, Stephanie Talbot had 14 points and Jackie Young totaled 14 points and 11 assists. Nneka Ogwumike, who was honored before the game, scored 17 points to lead the Sparks (16—27). Erica Wheeler added 16 points. The Aces used a 15-point run in the first quarter to take early control, going up 17-5. They led by 17 points when the Sparks went on their own long run, an 11-point spurt in the second period to cut the lead to 35-29. Los Angeles then remained within striking distance, but never closed the gap. Las Vegas' 10-point run in the third period put the Aces back in control with a 63-45 lead. The Aces presented Ogwumike, an eight-time All-Star and 2016 MVP, with a flower bouquet before the game. Ogwumike, who announced Aug. 19 she would retire after this season, also received a standing ovation from the crowd. She also is president of the players' union. Los Angeles played without Dearica Hamby (left knee) and Cameron Brink (right ankle). Hamby, who played in the Aces' organization from 2015-22, averages 14.4 points and 7.0 rebounds. Brink, the second overall pick in the 2024 draft, averages 9.5 points and 5.0 rebounds. Up next Sparks: Close their season Thursday night by hosting Golden State. Aces: End their regular season Thursday night at Phoenix. ------ See AP’s full WNBA coverage here
